description: This pie chart, related to the paper "Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse," illustrates the distribution of various media outlets across eighteen distinct categories. The segments are visually ordered by descending numerical value in a counter-clockwise direction, starting from the right side of the chart, and concluding with a general category at the bottom right. The chart includes the following slices: Breitbart (blue, 14), Drudge Report (orange, 8), The Daily Caller (green, 8), The Huffington Post (red, 7), NPR (purple, 6), Vox (brown, 6), The Guardian (pink, 5), BBC (grey, 5), RT (olive green, 4), Daily Kos (cyan, 3), National Review (blue, 3), Daily Mail (orange, 3), Red State (green, 3), Fox News (red, 3), CNN (purple, 3), PoliticusUSA (brown, 3), Shareblue (pink, 3), and Other (grey, unnumbered). Text labels identifying each media outlet are positioned outside the pie chart adjacent to their respective slices, while the numerical values are placed directly inside the colored segments. The chart does not utilize a separate legend, and no slices are visually emphasized by being exploded, offset, or bolded. Notably, the "Other" slice lacks an internal numerical label but contains a small, lighter grey rectangular artifact near its center.
